title: Health Literacy for Translated Patient Materials
summary: Improve translated patient materials with plain language, appropriate readability checks, patient testing, and a documented review workflow.
body_markdown:
###


There is no single reading level that works for every patient, language, or document. In United States healthcare settings, teams should use plain language, follow applicable organizational or program requirements, and test whether the intended audience can find, understand, and use the information.


###


No. English readability formulas measure features of English text and do not transfer directly to every language. For translated patient materials, use language-appropriate tools when available, review terminology and sentence structure, and test the material with people who use that language.


###


Interpretation supports a spoken conversation, while translation converts written patient education into another language. A translated handout does not replace interpretation when the patient needs to ask questions, and an interpreted explanation does not replace accurate written instructions for later use.


###


Test the material with members of the intended audience and ask them to locate key information, explain the main action, and describe what they would do next. In a United States healthcare workflow, document the language, version, reviewer feedback, revisions, approval date, and owner for future updates.


###


Opalite offers document translation alongside healthcare-specific AI interpretation across 150+ languages and dialects. A healthcare organization should still define the source text, terminology, formatting, approval, version control, and patient-testing workflow for each type of material.
